generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: FNA's account of the family: the leaves, at the base and on the stem, are distichous, so one stands at each node.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: FNA's account of the family: the leaves are distichous, in two ranks, their blades edgewise to the stem: an iris's fan.

traits.note: Michigan State's Botany Online account of the family, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): 6 petaloid tepals in two whorls, often united in a tube; stamens 3, opposite the outer tepals; ovary inferior (superior only in Tasmania's Isophysis), 3-locular, of 3 carpels. Iris and Sisyrinchium are regular (Sisyrinchium: the NEON biorepository's genus text, as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read); gladioli and their kin are zygomorphic.

traits.leaf_division.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 386 Iridaceae: leaves mostly narrowly linear, flattened sideways and sheathing (equitant); fruit a capsule opening by valves along its cells.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 386 Iridaceae: leaves mostly narrowly linear, flattened sideways and sheathing (equitant); fruit a capsule opening by valves along its cells.

traits.fruit_type.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 386 Iridaceae: leaves mostly narrowly linear, flattened sideways and sheathing (equitant); fruit a capsule opening by valves along its cells.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Iridaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Geosiridaceae: how long the leaves last (character 37), coded often evergreen, often deciduous. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Iridaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Geosiridaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded often a basal rosette, often no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Iridaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Geosiridaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Iridaceae with Geosiridaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, 231, 232, family Iridaceae: leaf venation parallel; read as "parallel".

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, 231, 232, family Iridaceae: inflorescence spike, solitary flower, or spike/panicle of rhipidia clusters, usually; read as {"panicle": "often", "solitary": "often", "spike": "often"}.
